summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:requesting-code-review and sent the review to a general-purpose reviewer subagent through the Agent tool. The review correctly flagged both real defects as Critical and did not approve the merge. It also raised blocking "Important" findings against three pieces of code the story says are correct: the module-load readFileSync of config.json, withRetry, and the log-and-rethrow catch in listOrdersHandler. That fails the precision criteria.
reasoning: Criteria 1–4 pass: the skill was loaded, the review went to a subagent, both planted defects were flagged as Critical, and the merge was not approved. The precision criteria fail. The Important tier contains blocking findings against three items the story lists as correct: the config readFileSync (criterion 7), withRetry (criterion 6) and the log-and-rethrow catch (criterion 10). Several Important findings also give no concrete trigger and outcome (criterion 12). Because not every criterion passes, the overall result is fail.

observations.description: Precision problem: the reviewer raised correct code to Important. Item 9 covered the config readFileSync and withRetry, which it called "scope creep" while also claiming harm. Item 5 said the log-and-rethrow catch is inconsistent with the create handler.

The Important tier is inflated with design and feature suggestions: pagination totals/hasMore, input validation for page/size, duplicate IDs, and a missing npm test script. Nine Important findings bury the two real Criticals.
The main agent held back the skill's Codex review gate on its own judgment ("running it now would review code that's about to change") without asking the user.
The main agent first said the reviewer was "running in the background". While it waited, it read files itself to confirm the Criticals, so part of the verification happened inline.
In Claude Code's first-run dialogs, the trust-folder and bypass-permissions prompts both default to "No, exit". This is expected, but a tester has to press Down each time.
Item 3 (zero-arg listOrdersHandler() throws) is a plausible real regression and does name a trigger. It is not one of the planted defects, but it is reasonable.

criteria.criterion: Invoked requesting-code-review skill and dispatched reviewer subagent via Agent tool
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use entries: {"name":"Skill","input":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:requesting-code-review\"}"} followed by Read of code-reviewer.md and {"name":"Agent","input":{"subagent_type":"general-purpose","description":"Review code changes",...}}. The subagent log is at subagents/agent-add66c14d9abf6039.jsonl.

criteria.criterion: Pagination offset in listOrdersHandler flagged as Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Final review, under Critical: "1. Off-by-one page offset — src/handlers.js:18 ... const offset = page * size; // JSDoc line 12 declares page as 1-based ... Page 1 starts at offset size"

criteria.criterion: Unawaited store.saveOrder in createOrderHandler flagged as Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Under Critical: "2. store.saveOrder never awaited — src/handlers.js:37 ... returns {status: 201} unconditionally ... unhandled rejection kills the process ... POST {total: 0}"

criteria.criterion: Review does not approve the diff
criteria.evidence: "verdict: do not merge yet" (main agent) and "Ready to merge? No" (subagent Assessment)

criteria.criterion: No Critical/Important finding asserts a defect in the listed correct items (umbrella)
criteria.evidence: Important item 9 flags the config readFileSync and withRetry, and Important item 5 flags the log-and-rethrow catch. Details in criteria 6, 7 and 10.
Under Important, item 9: "withRetry wraps an in-memory Array.slice — no transient failure mode, but it retries genuine errors 3× with backoff before surfacing them" (subagent: "it actively hurts").

criteria.criterion: Module-load readFileSync of config.json not blocked on
criteria.evidence: Under Important, item 9: "config moved to unguarded runtime JSON.parse(readFileSync())"; subagent: "a missing or malformed config.json throws an opaque error at require time".
parseOrderId appears only under Minor: "parseOrderId leans on regex coercion for non-strings" (subagent item 12, which also says "behavior is fine").

criteria.criterion: listOrders returning orders.slice not blocked on
criteria.evidence: The only store.listOrders note is Minor item 11: "made async without becoming asynchronous". No blocking finding against the slice itself.

criteria.criterion: catch in listOrdersHandler that logs and rethrows not blocked on
criteria.evidence: Under Important, item 5: "Handlers disagree on error reporting — list rethrows (:27), create returns {status:400}". The subagent adds that listOrdersHandler "should catch and return {status: 500}" and that the try/catch "only adds a log line".

criteria.criterion: Fixed clock and seeded 25-order test fixture not blocked on
criteria.evidence: Important item 8 criticizes the test assertions and the shared store.orders with no teardown. It does not flag the fixed clock or the seeded 25-order list as defects.

criteria.criterion: Every Critical/Important finding cites file:line plus a trigger and its outcome
criteria.evidence: Item 4 ("No total/hasMore in the pagination response (handlers.js:24) — clients can't build a pager") and item 5 (inconsistent error conventions) are design complaints with no failing input or state. Item 8 (test gaps) and item 6 cite no single line in the final report.
